# p-group　`def.p-group`
English entry · root `../`
[in graph](../#n=def.p-group)　·　[Chinese page (authoritative)](./def.p-group.md)

A subgroup $H \le G$ that is itself a $p$-group is a **$p$-subgroup**; of $G$, a maximal $p$-subgroup (under inclusion) is called a **Sylow $p$-subgroup**, see `def.sylow-subgroup`.

## Notes · **draft**
⭐ Examples: $\mathbb{Z}/p^{n}$, $V_4 = \mathbb{Z}/2 \times \mathbb{Z}/2$; the center of a $p$-group is nontrivial (a direct consequence of the class equation).

⚠ A $p$-group need not be abelian: $D_8$ (the dihedral group of order $8$) is a $2$-group but is not abelian.

⭐ A $p$-group is solvable, and in fact nilpotent: each step of its lower central series grows strictly and reaches $G$ in finitely many steps (the center is nontrivial, then induct on $G/Z$).
